title: Add Grafana dashboards + alerts for Dedicated burst pools (saturation, denials, tenant usage)
author: Sergio Costa
description: Summary: This PR adds the initial Grafana dashboard set and alert rules for Dedicated “burst capacity” pools. The focus is on (1) pool saturation visibility, (2) denial reason breakdowns that Support/CS can use to explain behavior, and (3) per-tenant burst usage/limits signals for debugging. Scope/Goals: - Dashboards: Burst Pool Overview (region + hardware class), Denials & Admission Health, Per-Tenant Burst Usage, and Neighbor Impact Indicators. - Alerts: pool saturation sustained, denial spike (by reason), admission controller error rate, telemetry lag guardrail, and global circuit breaker active. - Guardrails: enforce label/cardinality constraints (no raw tenant_id labels in default dashboards/alerts; tenant drill-down is via templated variables and restricted panels). - Runbook annotations: alert descriptions link to the burst overload mitigation runbook and include “what to check next” hints. Notes: This is intentionally “v1” for beta/GA readiness. Thresholds are conservative and will be tuned post-beta once we have stable baselines per region/hardware class. Related: - Data plane + admission controller metrics added in redwood PRs: pr-23822, pr-23919, pr-23988 - Metric taxonomy draft: burst-metrics-taxonomy (Drive) - Runbook: burst-pool-overload-mitigation-runbook (Confluence) Implementation details: - Grafana is maintained in jsonnet (grafonnet). Dashboards live under dashboards/dedicated/burst/*. - Alert rules are in prometheus_rule_groups/*.yaml and use existing alertmanager routing labels (team=sre, service=admission-controller, component=burst-pool). - Uses these primary metrics (names as emitted by redwood): redwood_burst_pool_saturation_ratio{region,hardware_class,pool} redwood_burst_admission_requests_total{decision,reason,region,hardware_class} redwood_burst_admission_latency_ms_bucket{region,hardware_class} redwood_burst_telemetry_lag_seconds{region,hardware_class,source} redwood_burst_global_circuit_breaker_active{region,hardware_class} redwood_dedicated_neighbor_p95_latency_delta_ms{region,hardware_class,route} (experimental panel only; not alerting yet) Dashboard inventory: 1) Dedicated / Burst Pools / Overview - Pool saturation over time (ratio + absolute available capacity when present) - Request vs admit vs deny rates - Top denial reasons (stacked) - Circuit breaker / fleet safety cap indicators 2) Dedicated / Burst Pools / Denials & Admission Health - Denials by reason (fleet_safety_cap, tenant_cap, cooldown, fairness_debt, pool_saturated, telemetry_stale, admission_timeout) - Admission controller p95 latency, error rate, timeout rate - Telemetry lag panel (by source) 3) Dedicated / Burst Pools / Tenant Usage (Restricted) - Template var: tenant (requires folder permission; intended for SRE/CS) - Burst usage (GPU-seconds) + burst tokens (if present) - Cap reached events (derived from denial reasons) - “last config change” panel (links to audit log search in control plane) 4) Dedicated / Burst Pools / Neighbor Impact (Experimental) - Non-burst p95 delta panel (by route) - Tail amplification proxy panel (if metric present) Alerts (initial thresholds): - BurstPoolSaturationHigh: saturation_ratio > 0.85 for 10m (severity=page when sustained in GA-enabled regions; severity=warn in beta regions via label gate) - BurstPoolDenialsSpike: increase(denials_total[5m]) / increase(requests_total[5m]) > 0.35 for 10m, excluding tenant_cap and cooldown reasons (these are expected) - BurstAdmissionControllerErrorRateHigh: 5xx or grpc_error_rate > 1% for 5m - BurstTelemetryLagHigh: telemetry_lag_seconds > 30 for 10m (warn) - BurstGlobalCircuitBreakerActive: circuit_breaker_active == 1 for 2m (page) Known limitations / follow-ups: - No per-tenant alerting in v1 (intentional). We’ll revisit after we confirm tenant_id hashing / cardinality budget with Telemetry Platform. - Neighbor impact signals are experimental and NOT used for automated rollback gating yet (tracked in ENG-23988/related redwood work). - Region/hardware allowlist gating is expected to be handled in redwood rollout flags; this PR adds optional labels to silence alerts in non-enabled regions. Testing: - jsonnetfmt + grafonnet build outputs validated locally - promtool check rules passed - Rendered dashboards imported into staging Grafana; verified templating and variable queries against staging Prometheus.
commits: dashboards: add burst pool overview + denial breakdown panels
alerts: add saturation/denial spike/telemetry lag rules with runbook annotations
dashboards: add restricted per-tenant usage dashboard (templated variable)
chore: jsonnet linting and folder permissions guidance
review_conversation: Allison Grant (review): Please confirm we are not introducing tenant_id as a metric label anywhere in default panels/alerts. We need to keep cardinality bounded; tenant drill-down should be templated variable only and ideally folder-restricted.

Sergio Costa (author): Confirmed. No tenant_id label usage. Tenant dashboard uses a variable that queries a control-plane-derived allowlist and then filters on tenant_slug (not id) via dashboard variable, and the panels are in a restricted folder. Alerts have no tenant scoping.
Logan Wright (review): Denial spike alert: can we exclude expected reasons like tenant_cap/cooldown? Otherwise we’ll page on healthy behavior when customers hit their configured caps.
Sergio Costa (author): Updated rule to compute deny_ratio excluding tenant_cap + cooldown. Added a separate non-paging “BurstTenantCapDenialsHigh” recording rule for visibility only (no alert).
Sean Gallagher (review): Add runbook links + first steps in annotations. Also, for saturation alert, please use 10m to avoid paging on short spikes during autoscaler scale-out.

Sergio Costa (author): Done. Added runbook URLs and a short checklist in annotations. Saturation now requires 10m sustained. Also added an alert annotation to check circuit breaker and telemetry lag first.

Peter Holtz (review): The circuit breaker active alert should page fast (2m) but include a hint to check fleet safety caps and recent rollout toggles. Can we also include region/hardware labels in the summary?
Sergio Costa (author): Added region/hardware_class to summary/description. Included suggested checks (fleet cap, rollout gate, recent config change).
Allison Grant (approval): LGTM after the tenant label/cardinality changes. Please keep neighbor impact dashboard marked experimental and do not alert off it yet.
Sean Gallagher (approval): LGTM. This should be good enough for beta; we’ll tune thresholds during game day and first week of dogfood.
release_notes: Added Dedicated burst capacity Grafana dashboards and initial alert rules for saturation, denials, telemetry lag, and circuit breaker state. Includes restricted per-tenant drill-down dashboard for SRE/CS.
